title: A unified closed-form theory for elastic waves in polycrystals of any crystal symmetry
authors: Ming Huang, Stanislav I. Rokhlin, Michael J. S. Lowe
abstract: arXiv:2611.26674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The coherent elastic wave in random polycrystals is described by the first-order smoothing approximation, whose mass operator remains an integral evaluated only numerically. Here we derive its closed form for equiaxed, untextured polycrystals of any crystal symmetry with an exponential correlation function, giving an explicit dispersion equation at all frequencies. Unlike the integral form, which fails beyond one inverse correlation radius from the real axis, the closed form holds deep in the complex wavenumber plane, where heavily attenuated roots lie. It is compact, reproduces the dispersion equations of Stanke and Kino for cubic grains, extends them to any symmetry and contains the Born and far-field approximations as special cases. It reveals the structure of the roots and their partitions of the coherent field: three roots per polarization, one from the incident wave and one from each of the two scattering channels, without and with mode conversion. It also yields closed-form limits of their velocity, attenuation and partition in the Rayleigh, stochastic and geometric regimes, which show why a single coherent wave has been observed at long wavelengths, whereas more than one can be observed at short wavelengths. These results underpin further theory and quantitative characterization of polycrystalline microstructure.
summary:
- Closed‑form mass operator for coherent elastic waves in equiaxed, untextured polycrystals of any symmetry, yielding an explicit dispersion equation valid at all frequencies.
- Extends Stanke–Kino cubic‑grain results, includes Born and far‑field limits, and shows three coherent roots per polarization (incident + two scattering channels with/without mode conversion).
- Gives closed‑form limits for velocity, attenuation, and partition in Rayleigh, stochastic, and geometric regimes, explaining the transition from a single to multiple coherent waves with wavelength.

title: Topologically Obstructed Kondo Hybridization: A Route to Kondo Semimetals
authors: Yue Liu, Junze Deng, Haoyu Hu
abstract: arXiv:2611.26686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay of strong correlations, topology, and symmetry can reshape the low-energy electronic structure of quantum materials and drive the emergence of novel quantum phases. In heavy-fermion systems, the Kondo effect entangles localized $f$ moments with conduction electrons, giving rise to coherent heavy-electron bands at low temperatures, typically characterized by a Kondo hybridization gap. Here we show, however, that the topology and symmetry of the conduction-electron Fermi surface can obstruct the opening of the Kondo hybridization gap at certain momenta. Treating the Fermi surface of a three-dimensional system as an effective two-dimensional manifold, we demonstrate that nontrivial topological invariants defined on this manifold impose a topological obstruction to opening a full hybridization gap, forcing the $fc$ hybridization to vanish at certain momenta on the Fermi surface. These hybridization zeros lead to crossings between $c$ and $f$ bands, giving rise to nodal points or lines near the Fermi energy within the Kondo phase. Our results establish topological obstructions to Kondo hybridization as a route to Kondo semimetals, revealing a fundamental connection between Fermi-surface topology and the emergence of correlated electronic phases.
summary:
- Topological invariants of the conduction‑electron Fermi surface can forbid a full Kondo hybridization gap, forcing hybridization zeros at specific momenta.
- Hybridization zeros produce c‑f band crossings, yielding nodal points or lines near the Fermi energy within the Kondo phase.
- This mechanism offers a route to Kondo semimetals, linking Fermi‑surface topology to emergent correlated phases.

title: Off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing in one dimension from critical density fluctuations
authors: Matthew D. Thomson, Simon M. Martin, Frank Marsiglio, Joseph Maciejko
abstract: arXiv:2611.26690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central theme in the theory of unconventional superconductivity is that Cooper pairing can be mediated by bosonic collective modes other than lattice vibrations. However, collective fluctuations in reduced dimensions can also have a destabilizing effect on superconductivity, by suppressing long-range order or by destroying Fermi-liquid quasiparticles in the normal state. In this work, we study a one-dimensional (1D) model of spinless fermions with local interactions that exhibits a continuous quantum phase transition from a Luttinger liquid to a phase-separated state. Combining field-theoretic arguments with numerical exact diagonalization and matrix-product-state methods, we find that the quantum critical point exhibits two-particle off-diagonal long-range order and $p$-wave pairing. Our work shows that critical density fluctuations at a phase-separation instability can act as pairing glue for unconventional superconductivity in 1D, overcoming the disordering effect of phase fluctuations and the absence of long-lived fermionic quasiparticles in the normal state.
summary:
- 1D spinless fermion model shows a continuous transition from a Luttinger liquid to phase separation.
- At the quantum critical point, two‑particle off‑diagonal long‑range order and $p$‑wave pairing emerge.
- Critical density fluctuations near phase‑separation act as pairing glue, overcoming disordering effects of phase fluctuations.

title: Topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry
abstract: arXiv:2611.26693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral (or sublattice) symmetry describes bipartite systems such as the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain where same-sublattice A-A and B-B hoppings are forbidden, enabling the protection of topological phases. Here we identify new topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry wherein chiral symmetry is preserved on only one sublattice, as may occur with sublattice imbalance (e.g. graphene-hBN) or localized orbitals (e.g. zincblende). Unlike conventional symmetry operators described by group theory, half-chiral symmetry is an algebraic constraint on the sublattice-projected Hamiltonian such as $PHP=0$, requiring a new framework for topological protection. We develop such a framework, identifying real-space bulk topological invariants and corresponding topological boundary modes that stick to zero energy. In two dimensions we construct a half-chiral Kekule honeycomb model and show that its unusual higher-order topology protects a single zero-energy mode at a single corner.
summary:
- Introduces “half‑chiral symmetry,” where chiral symmetry acts only on one sublattice, enabling new topological phases.
- Builds an algebraic framework with real‑space bulk invariants and predicts zero‑energy boundary modes.
- Shows a 2D half‑chiral Kekulé honeycomb model hosts a higher‑order topological corner state at a single corner.

title: When the magnetic force theorem fails: dressed exchange in the induced-moment magnets FePt, FePd, CoPt, and CoPd
authors: Vladislav Borisov, Maryna Pankratova, Rohit Pathak, Pamela Costa Carvalho, Erna K. Delczeg-Czirjak, Sagar Sarkar, Anders Bergman, Qichen Xu, Nezhat Pournaghavi, Manuel Pereiro, Hermann D\"urr, Mikhail I. Katsnelson, Olle Eriksson, Anna Delin
abstract: arXiv:2611.26697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Effective spin Hamiltonians for itinerant magnets are commonly parameterized by magnetic-force-theorem (MFT) exchange constants, which are subsequently used to compute the behavior of complex and delicate spin textures, for example skyrmions. We show that for systems containing atoms with large spin susceptibility, such as Pd or Pt, this approach misses important parts of the energetics. For FePt, it even predicts the wrong ground state. Benchmarking against fully self-consistent spin-spiral density-functional calculations - in which the electronic structure, including the induced Pd/Pt moments, relaxes for every spin configuration - we quantify the missing energetics for the ordered L1$_0$ alloys FePt, FePd, CoPt, and CoPd. By comparing a family of models that differ only in their treatment of the induced Pt moment, including the configuration-dependent models of Mryasov and Polesya, we identify the origin: the energetics of the induced moments are governed by the exchange-enhanced (dressed) susceptibility, of which the frozen-potential MFT captures only the bare part - about one third of the Pt-mediated interaction in FePt. We derive a general bound showing that no on-site (intra-atomic) refinement can supply the missing strength. The dressing decides the magnetic ground state in FePt, where the interlayer ordering rests entirely on the Pt-mediated interactions, and shifts the Curie temperatures of the other alloys by several hundred kelvin. Computed ordering temperatures, magnon spectra and spin wave stiffness for all four compounds are provided.
summary:
- MFT exchange constants miss induced Pd/Pt moment energetics, mispredicting FePt’s ground state.
- Self‑consistent spin‑spiral DFT shows Pt’s dressed susceptibility supplies ~⅔ of the Pt‑mediated interaction, absent in frozen‑potential MFT.
- Accounting for dressed moments corrects Curie temperatures and determines magnetic ordering in FePt, FePd, CoPt, CoPd.

title: Large deviations, effective dynamics, and dynamical phase transitions in random maps
authors: \'Angela Tajuelo-Valbuena, Jorge Hidalgo, Ricardo Guti\'errez, Carlos P\'erez-Espigares
abstract: arXiv:2611.26704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large deviation theory provides a natural framework to characterize rare fluctuations of time-averaged observables in deterministic and stochastic systems. Building on previous results for deterministic chaotic maps, here we extend the Doob transform to random maps, constructing an effective dynamics in which rare events become typical. This makes it possible to directly reproduce the dynamics of rare trajectories that are exponentially difficult to sample under the original dynamics. We further apply spectral large-deviation methods to characterize dynamical phase transitions in random maps. The spectral structure of the tilted operator provides insight into the mechanisms underlying these transitions and, in particular, allows us to identify the appropriate initial states that select one dynamical phase or another. Our results extend the connection between large deviation theory, spectral methods, and effective dynamics to random chaotic maps, providing a general framework to study rare events and dynamical phase transitions in these systems.
summary:
- Extends Doob transform to random maps, enabling rare events to become typical in an effective dynamics.
- Applies spectral large‑deviation analysis to identify dynamical phase transitions and the initial states that select each phase.
- Establishes a general framework linking large deviations, spectral methods, and effective dynamics for random chaotic maps.

title: Free-Space Excitation of Frozen Waves and Topological Edge States in Graphene at a Time Interface
authors: Shivaksh Rawat, Samyobrata Mukherjee, Jeffery W. Allen, Monica S. Allen, Gennady Shvets
abstract: arXiv:2611.26714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-varying two-dimensional materials, such as graphene under ultrafast photoexcitation, offer a promising platform for engineering temporal interfaces for electromagnetic waves. Rapidly promoting valence electrons to the conduction band generates a high-energy, non-thermal hot-electron population that subsequently thermalizes with the pre-existing thermal electron population. We study the excitation of plasmonic modes in graphene by the time interface created by ultra-fast photoexcitation using a graphene electron-transport model that is self-consistently coupled to electromagnetic simulations. We find that in addition to dynamic, propagating plasmonic modes, the time interfaces result in the excitation of static, spatially varying electromagnetic modes in the interaction region sustained by streaming transverse electrons. We also demonstrate a novel technique for coupling free-space light directly to highly localized topological edge states at the magnetic-inversion boundary on graphene, eliminating the need for near-field excitation techniques.
summary:
- Ultrafast photoexcitation of graphene forms a time interface that excites both propagating plasmons and static, spatially varying modes sustained by streaming electrons.
- A self‑consistent electron‑transport model coupled to EM simulations captures these time‑interface–induced phenomena.
- The work enables direct free‑space coupling to localized topological edge states at a magnetic‑inversion boundary, eliminating near‑field excitation.

title: Impact of spin fluctuations on spectral functions and transport in a model altermagnet
authors: Sourav Chakraborty, Manoranjan Kumar, Arun Paramekanti
abstract: arXiv:2611.26725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding spin dependent transport in altermagnets is important for incorporating them in next generation spintronic technologies. Motivated by the discovery of altermagnetism in strongly correlated quantum materials, we explore this physics in the checkerboard lattice Hubbard model using a fermion Monte Carlo approach which tracks the full spatial dependence of spin fluctuations as a function of temperature. We present results for the evolution of the spin-dependent single particle spectral functions and transport as we go from the ordered ground state into the high temperature disordered paramagnetic phase. Our results could be tested in future spin-selective angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin transport experiments in candidate altermagnets realized in solid state quantum materials or in proposed ultracold atomic systems.
summary:
- Explores spin‑dependent transport in altermagnets via a checkerboard lattice Hubbard model using fermion Monte Carlo.
- Tracks temperature‑dependent spin fluctuations and their impact on single‑particle spectral functions and transport.
- Provides predictions for spin‑selective ARPES and spin‑transport experiments in solid‑state or ultracold atomic altermagnets.

title: Atomic layer etching of niobium via alternating O$_2$ and H$_2$/SF$_6$ plasma exposures
authors: Lillian B. Hughes Wyatt, Azmain A. Hossain, Yifei Yan, Austin J. Minnich
abstract: arXiv:2611.26735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Niobium thin films are a key component of superconducting detectors and electronics, and film surface quality, surface roughness, and geometrical dimensional accuracy affect many performance metrics. Atomic layer etching (ALE) is of interest for modifying film surfaces owing to its Angstrom-scale etching precision and surface smoothing characteristics. Here, we report a plasma-enhanced ALE process for Nb based on sequential O$_2$ plasma and H$_2$/SF$_6$ plasma exposures. The process achieves an etch per cycle of 5-7 Angstrom/cycle and exhibits surface smoothing. The superconducting transition temperature of the ALE-treated films is maintained up to the expected decrease associated with reduced film thickness. Our ALE process could find applications in superconducting electronics for which surface quality and precise thickness control are of high importance.
summary:
- Developed a plasma‑enhanced ALE for Nb using alternating O₂ and H₂/SF₆ plasmas.
- Achieved 5–7 Å per cycle with surface smoothing and preserved superconducting Tc.
- Enables precise thickness control for high‑quality superconducting detectors and electronics.

title: Emergent Long-Range Entanglement in the XXZ Quantum Spin Chain with Competing Orders
authors: Anthony Balchin, Eytan Grosfeld, Eran Ginossar
abstract: arXiv:2611.26741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Competition between short-range and long-range interactions is a largely unexplored route to one-dimensional quantum matter. We introduce a spin-1/2 XXZ chain with ferromagnetic nearest-neighbour and antiferromagnetic power-law couplings. Using DMRG and spin-wave theory, we show this competition stabilises a gapless phase with central charge $c=0.997(17)$, a twofold-degenerate ground state and entanglement spectrum, absent in nearest-neighbour models, and is long-range entangled as diagnosed by finite quantum conditional mutual information. The model also generates a unique gapped quantum phase and gapless antiphase with non-decaying correlations.
summary:
- XXZ spin‑½ chain with ferromagnetic nearest‑neighbour and antiferromagnetic power‑law couplings.
- Gapless phase: central charge ≈ 1, twofold‑degenerate ground state, entanglement spectrum, long‑range entanglement (finite conditional mutual information).
- Additional unique gapped phase and a gapless antiphase with non‑decaying correlations.

title: Geometric Contribution to the Electron-Phonon Coupling Constant: Checkerboard and Hyper-diamond Models
authors: Thomas Caligiure, Daniel P. Arovas, Jiabin Yu
abstract: arXiv:2611.26823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent theoretical studies on electron-phonon coupling (EPC) - a key ingredient in the emergence of diverse quantum phases such as superconductivity and charge-density waves - have revealed a distinct contribution to its strength arising from the quantum geometry of electronic bands. Here we investigate the quantum geometric contribution, characterized by the quantum metric, to the dimensionless EPC constant in the checkerboard and hyper-diamond models, under the Gaussian approximation. We show that in the checkerboard model, the geometric contribution can be tuned independently while keeping the energetic part fixed, demonstrating the possibility of enhancing EPC strength through quantum geometry. In the hyper-diamond model, the geometric contribution accounts for roughly $50\%$ of the total EPC constant across all spatial dimensions, generalizing the $d=2$ result for graphene to higher dimensions.
summary:
- Quantum metric provides an independent, tunable contribution to electron‑phonon coupling (EPC) in the checkerboard lattice.
- In the checkerboard model, this geometric term can be enhanced while the energetic part remains fixed, boosting overall EPC.
- For the hyper‑diamond lattice, the geometric contribution accounts for ~50 % of the total EPC in any dimension, extending the graphene result to higher‑dimensional systems.

title: Majorana quasiparticles, mass hierarchies, and the phase diagram of the Gross-Neveu model in D=2+1
abstract: arXiv:2611.26872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the canonical $2+1$-dimensional $O(2N)$-symmetric Gross-Neveu model with the inversion-breaking mass-term features a sequence of $O(2N-k) \times O(k)$ - symmetric ground states in its zero-temperature phase diagram, with $k=1,...,N$. For odd $k$ the quasiparticle excitations are itinerant, massive, two-real-component Majorana fermions, i.e. half of Dirac fermions. The solutions of the mean-field equations symmetric under $O(2N-k_1-k_2) \times O(k_1) \times O(k_2)$ with $k_1, k_2 \geq 1$ also exist, but are found to be unstable. Some manifestations of Majorana quasiparticle in the particular ``uniaxial nematic" state with $k=1$ are outlined, and analogies to other physical systems are offered.
summary:
- 2+1‑D O(2N) Gross‑Neveu model with inversion‑breaking mass exhibits a zero‑temperature sequence of O(2N‑k) × O(k) symmetric ground states for k = 1,…,N.
- For odd k the quasiparticles are itinerant, massive Majorana fermions (half a Dirac fermion).
- The uniaxial nematic (k = state shows Majorana signatures; other O(2N‑k₁‑k₂) × O(k₁) × O(k₂) solutions are unstable.

title: Quantum order by disorder among lozenge tilings: a staircase of hub-free crystals between the Lieb ferrimagnet and the antiferromagnet
authors: Suhwan Yoo, Jeehoon Choi, Chaeyeon Kim, Hee Young Kwon, Changyeon Won
abstract: arXiv:2611.27076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lozenge tilings of the triangular lattice define an exponentially large family of bipartite networks, from the dice lattice, a Lieb ferrimagnet with the largest sublattice imbalance, to square-type tilings, which are compensated antiferromagnets. For the classical Heisenberg antiferromagnet all of them are degenerate. We show that quantum fluctuations lift this degeneracy through a local mechanism: the zero-point energy is, to leading order, a sum of site terms that are convex in the coordination $z$, so that Jensen's inequality at fixed $\langle z\rangle=4$ selects the square-type tiling. An expansion about the Ising limit explains the convexity: a site with more bonds has more channels for quantum fluctuations, but each fluctuation frustrates more bonds. A magnetic field couples to the Lieb moment and competes with this selection. Because the moment is carried most cheaply by threefold and fivefold sites, sixfold hubs are avoided, and bond counting together with the Lieb--Mattis theorem limits hub-free tilings to $3/5$ of the dice moment. Quantum Monte Carlo and a complete enumeration of periodic tilings with small unit cells show that the classical jump is replaced by a staircase of periodic crystals. Its widest step is a hub-free crystal that saturates the bound; below it, threefold and fivefold defects pack ever more densely in a shallow sequence of crystals, controlled by a short-ranged attraction between defects of equal curvature and a repulsion between defects of opposite curvature. Selection energies scale as $JS$. In the height representation the coordination is the discrete Gaussian curvature and the Lieb moment its sublattice-staggered part. We give spectroscopic signatures and discuss realizations in nanographenes, atomic spin arrays and quantum simulators.
summary:
- Quantum fluctuations lift the classical degeneracy of lozenge‑tiling networks, selecting square‑type tilings through a convex zero‑point energy that depends on site coordination.
- A magnetic field couples to the Lieb moment, favoring three‑ and five‑fold sites and suppressing six‑fold hubs, limiting hub‑free tilings to 3/5 of the dice‑lattice moment.
- The classical jump is replaced by a staircase of periodic crystals: the widest step is a hub‑free crystal saturating the bound, followed by progressively denser three‑/five‑fold defect crystals.

title: Kinetic Arrest of a Disordered First-Order Phase Transition in Strained V2O3 Thin Films
abstract: arXiv:2611.27168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a continuum phenomenological theory for the kinetic arrest (KA) of a first-order phase transition (FOPT), taking the thermal and electric field-driven metal-insulator transition (MIT) in epitaxial V2O3 thin films as a prototype. By defining a coarse-grained mesoscopic order parameter representing the metallic volume fraction coupled to the primary structural monoclinic distortion, we formulate a Time-Dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) framework integrated with a non-local elastic interaction kernel and an Imry-Wortis quenched disorder landscape. We derive an explicit dynamic criterion for the kinetic arrest boundary TK(E) by analyzing the divergence of the intrinsic order-parameter relaxation time relative to experimental observation timescales. Our framework rigorously decouples the thermodynamic driving force from the kinetic activation barrier. We demonstrate that epitaxial substrate-induced clamping elevates local elastic barriers, pinning domain boundaries and stabilizing an arrested, inhomogeneous mosaic of metallic and insulating phases down to cryogenic temperatures. The simulated transformation kinetics exhibit an Avrami exponent suppression to values n < 1, reflecting slow, hindered domain-wall propagation. Furthermore, we examine the effect of an external electric field as an isothermal mechanism that lowers this kinetic barrier, providing a phenomenological description of threshold de-arrest and multi-level resistance states. We critically discuss this electronic barrier-lowering mechanism in comparison with electrothermal Joule heating, establish diagnostic criteria to distinguish them, and contextualize these non-equilibrium dynamics with related phenomena in disordered superconducting films.
summary:
- TDGL model couples metallic volume fraction to monoclinic distortion, including elastic kernel and disorder, to capture kinetic arrest in strained V₂O₃ films.
- Derived T_K(E) criterion shows substrate clamping raises elastic barriers, yielding a mosaic of phases with Avrami exponent n <
- External electric field lowers the kinetic barrier, enabling threshold de‑arrest and multi‑level switching of the transition.

title: Nonmonotonic Magnetic Correlations in Decorated Lieb-Lattice Anderson Models
authors: Raymond Hmuifoo, Edwin W. Huang, Annabelle Ancheta, Richard T. Scalettar
abstract: arXiv:2611.27247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay between electronic correlations and lattice geometry can strongly modify the competition between magnetic correlations and local singlet formation in multiorbital Hamiltonians. Here we use determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations to investigate two periodic Anderson-like models constructed by selectively hybridizing localized orbitals to the inequivalent sites of a Lieb lattice. The resulting geometries possess partially filled flat bands and different sublattice imbalances. We examine the evolution of local spin correlations and orbital-resolved magnetic structure factors as the hybridization is increased. Although correlations between hybridized orbitals evolve relatively smoothly toward local singlet formation, the longer-range magnetic correlations exhibit a striking nonmonotonic dependence on hybridization. In particular, we observe a pronounced suppression at intermediate hybridization followed by a substantial recovery on undecorated lattice sites. We discuss these results in relation to earlier studies of depleted periodic Anderson models and the constraints imposed by Lieb's theorem. Our findings illustrate how selective hybridization and flat-band structure can produce unusual redistributions of magnetic correlations in strongly interacting multiorbital systems.
summary:
- QMC on Lieb‑lattice Anderson models with selective hybridization → flat bands, sublattice imbalance.
- Local singlet formation smooth; long‑range magnetism nonmonotonic: dip at intermediate hybridization, then recovery on undecorated sites.
- Demonstrates flat‑band geometry redistributes magnetic correlations, extending insights from depleted Anderson models and Lieb’s theorem.

title: Role of antisite disorder in dictating the Ising anisotropy and ferromagnetic ground state of NdGaSi
authors: Anyesh Saraswati, Sourav Kanthal, Subhajit Nandy, Jhuma Sannigrahi, Matthias Gutmann, Nitesh Kumar
abstract: arXiv:2611.27334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single-ion anisotropy and exchange interactions together set the magnetic ground state of rare-earth intermetallics, yet the role of chemical disorder on the ligand sublattice remains little explored. Here, we show that Ga/Si antisite disorder in NdGaSi stabilises the centrosymmetric $I4_1/amd$ structure and raises the Nd$^{3+}$ site symmetry to $D_{2d}$, which forbids all $m=\pm2$ Stevens operators in the crystalline electric field (CEF) Hamiltonian. Magnetization, specific heat, single-crystal neutron diffraction, and x-ray absorption spectroscopy establish the disordered structure and a collinear ferromagnetic order below $T_\mathrm{C}\approx11$~K with Ising anisotropy along $c$. A CEF analysis that fits the susceptibilities along both axes and the magnetic specific heat simultaneously yields a ground-state doublet that is $\sim97\%$ pure, in contrast to the strongly mixed ground state of the Al/Si-ordered NdAlSi ($C_{2v}$ site symmetry of Nd$^{3+}$). We argue that this ground-state purity makes the ordered moment rigid against the modulation due to frustrated exchange, selecting a $\mathbf{k}=0$ ferromagnet in NdGaSi instead of the incommensurate ferrimagnet of NdAlSi. Antisite disorder, thus, acts as a handle on CEF ground-state purity and can, thereby, select between fundamentally different magnetic ground states.
summary:
- Ga/Si antisite disorder stabilizes the centrosymmetric I4₁/amd structure, raising Nd³⁺ site symmetry to D₂d and forbidding m = ±2 Stevens operators.
- The resulting ~97 % pure ground‑state doublet yields a collinear ferromagnet with Ising anisotropy along c below T_C ≈ 11 K.
- This CEF purity selects a k = 0 ferromagnetic ground state, contrasting the incommensurate ferrimagnet of ordered NdAlSi, demonstrating disorder as a tuning knob for magnetic order.
